1. **P2 â€” Raw-disk ancestry can bypass refusal and the authorization snapshot.** [discover.py:2037](C:/Users/Jack/beamo-release-work/20261024-wipe-audit-pass2/src/beamo_wipe/discover.py:2037), [safety.py:644](C:/Users/Jack/beamo-release-work/20261024-wipe-audit-pass2/src/beamo_wipe/safety.py:644).

   Reproduction: authorize an unmounted 500 GB `/dev/sda` with unique serial/WWN and boot `/dev/sdz`. At final rediscovery, change only the target row to include `"pkname": "sdz"`. The target remains selectable; target and inventory snapshots remain equal; boot exclusion and rediscovery checks pass. Exact `NwipeRunner.start()` reaches the fake `Popen` recorder with `--exclude=/dev/sdz` and `/dev/sda`. An unknown parent also reaches that boundary. Nested observations beneath mounted storage reproduce the same omission; a directly mounted target is correctly refused.

   **Impact:** contradictory or unresolved physical ancestry does not reliably fail closed. This requires malformed observations; I have not demonstrated a normal kernel producing this raw-disk topology or any real erasure. Refuse eligible raw-disk rows with unresolved, cyclic or protected ancestry before authorization and execution.

2. **P2 â€” Local NVMe failover can hide an otherwise available target.** [safety.py:795](C:/Users/Jack/beamo-release-work/20261024-wipe-audit-pass2/src/beamo_wipe/safety.py:795).

   Reproduction: model namespace head `nvme0n1` served by two PCIe controllers, `nvme0` and `nvme1`. Both initially pass. Remove only the fake `nvme0/transport` file while retaining the namespace and surviving `nvme1` PCIe path. Discovery returns no selectable target; launch refuses with `Cannot prove NVMe is locally attached`. The implementation reads only the controller name inferred from the namespace prefix.

   Linux 6.1 names namespace heads using the subsystem instance and retains that instance after the original controller disappears. Resolve the namespaceâ€™s surviving controllers through sysfs instead of assuming matching numbers. This is a kernel-source-supported availability scenario, reproduced only with fake sysfs. [Kernel naming](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.1/drivers/nvme/host/multipath.c), [instance lifetime](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/refs/tags/v6.1/drivers/nvme/host/core.c).

   **The earlier unrelated-controller bypass hypothesis is withdrawn:** Linuxâ€™s instance reservation rules out the supplied topology.

The original findingâ€”whole-log assessment can succeed while the authenticated suffix cannot substantiate recovery/exportâ€”is already accepted for proof outside the retained window. A separate, bounded race is reproducible:

1. Poll A caches the complete 10,209-byte terminal log and assessment.
2. Poll Bâ€™s progress refresh overwrites `_log_tail` with 8,000 bytes.
3. A publishes success and clears `_proc`.
4. B discards its subsequent completion read because `_proc` changed.
5. Exact `_write_evidence` capture retains the 8,000-byte suffix alongside the 10,209-byte assessment.

Observed results:

```text

serial                 10209      10209     completed           completed
concurrent polls        8000      10209     completed           completion_missing
```

Recovery consequently refuses success; export rejects its completion claim. This needs neither a >1 MiB log nor disk I/O in the reproduction.

**Reachability objection:** neither `get_log_tail` nor `_remember_log_snapshot` exists in the specified source. The writer is `_refresh_progress`. [Wizard tick holds its lock across polling](C:/Users/Jack/beamo-release-work/20261024-wipe-audit-pass2/src/beamo_wipe/wizard.py:875); Stop claims `STOPPING` under that same lock before its worker polls. Those callers prevent the demonstrated overlap. Thus this is a confirmed runner concurrency hazard, not yet a demonstrated shipped-flow P2.

Minimal defensive recommendation: under the existing runner lock, prevent progress refreshes from replacing `_log_tail` once `_assessment_ready` is published. Preserve the separate whole-log assessment, exact bounded suffix, privacy checks, and recovery/export authentication. **Do not switch assessment to suffix-only:** the inert negative control returned `engine_failed` for the whole log but `completed` for its suffix.

live = p.read_bytes()
def reader_span(b):
    c = next(n for n in ast.parse(b).body if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and n.name == "NwipeRunner")
    n = next(n for n in c.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == "_read_log_tail")
    return n.lineno - 1, n.end_lineno
a, z = reader_span(entry); x, y = reader_span(live)
b = b"".join(entry.splitlines(True)[:a] + live.splitlines(True)[x:y] + entry.splitlines(True)[z:])
assert hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest() == "7787976b2084d6a01b1df2e86b16cc3154b8b29e5ed0b8ac9655da1df95ff345"
t = ast.parse(b)
c = next(n for n in t.body if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and n.name == "NwipeRunner")
selected = [n for n in t.body if (
    isinstance(n, (ast.Assign, ast.AnnAssign)) and (45 <= n.lineno < 163 or 648 <= n.lineno < 1240)
    or isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and 648 <= n.lineno < 1240)]
methods = [n for n in c.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name in
           {"poll", "_refresh_progress", "_complete_log_records", "_update_progress"}]
selected.append(ast.ClassDef(name="Runner", bases=[], keywords=[], body=methods, decorator_list=[]))
future = ast.parse("from __future__ import annotations").body
ns = dict(re=re, math=math, os=S(path=posixpath), WipeResult=lambda **k: S(**k),
          SafetyError=RuntimeError, ProcessStatusError=RuntimeError, _try_log_diag=lambda *a: None,
          METHODS={"everyday": S(verify="last", overwrite_passes=1, rounds=1)})
exec(compile(ast.fix_missing_locations(ast.Module(body=future + selected, type_ignores=[])), str(p), "exec"), ns)
sys.modules["beamo_wipe"] = types.ModuleType("beamo_wipe")
progress = types.ModuleType("beamo_wipe.progress"); progress.observe = lambda *a: None
sys.modules["beamo_wipe.progress"] = progress
classify = ns["completion_for_method"]
proof = ns["NWIPE_DRIVE_STATUS_HEADER"] + "\n      sda | Erased | 120MB/s | 01:25:04 | FAKE\n"
log = proof + "x" * (10208 - len(proof)) + "\n"
request = S(device="/dev/sda", method="everyday", logfile="in-memory")
def run(race):
    r = ns["Runner"]()
    r.__dict__.update(_lock=threading.Lock(), _proc=S(poll=lambda: 0), _active_request=request,
        _status_polling=None, _progress_read_seq=0, _log_read_state=threading.local(),
        result=None, progress=None, _log_tail="", _release_wipe_lock=lambda: None)
    refreshed, done = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
    failures = []
    def wait(event):
        assert event.wait(3), "bounded probe wait expired"
    def read(path, count):
        r._log_read_state.truncated = False
        if race and threading.current_thread() is later and count == 1048576:
            refreshed.set(); wait(done)
        return log[-count:]
    def second():
        try:
            r.poll(request)
        except BaseException as exc:
            failures.append(repr(exc))
    later = threading.Thread(target=second)
    def assess(*args):
        result = classify(*args)
        if race and threading.current_thread() is not later:
            later.start(); wait(refreshed)
        return result
    r._read_log_tail = read; ns["completion_for_method"] = assess
    try:
        r.poll(request)
    finally:
        done.set()
        if later.ident is not None:
            later.join(5)
    assert not later.is_alive() and not failures, failures
    print(race, r.result.reason, len(r._log_tail), len(r._assessment_log_text),
          classify(0, r._log_tail, "/dev/sda", "everyday")[2])
run(False); run(True)
negative = "/dev/sda: >>> FAILURE! <<<\n" + "x" * 10000 + "\n" + proof
print("negative:", classify(0, negative, "/dev/sda", "everyday")[2],
      classify(0, negative[-8000:], "/dev/sda", "everyday")[2])

Linux 6.1 permits this layout: with multipath enabled and a private namespace lacking the unique-NSID guarantees, it creates no multipath head, names the disk using the subsystem instance, and parents it under its actual controller. Thus `nvme0n2` can legitimately belong directly to `nvme1` in `nvme-subsys0`. This follows from [nvme_is_unique_nsid](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.1/drivers/nvme/host/nvme.h), [head allocation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.1/drivers/nvme/host/multipath.c), and [namespace naming/parenting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.1/drivers/nvme/host/core.c).
